title: git interactive rebase autosquash
body: Use `git rebase -i --autosquash` to let fixup!/squash! commit subjects in your history be reordered and merged automatically. Without --autosquash the fixup commits stay where you made them and you have to move them by hand.

title: git rerere reuse recorded resolution
body: `git rerere` records how you resolved a hunk once and replays it the next time the same conflict appears. Enable globally with `git config --global rerere.enabled true` so merges across long-lived branches stop asking you to redo work.

title: git bisect run for automated bug hunts
body: When `git bisect run <script>` exits non-zero on the broken commit and zero on the good one, git walks the range for you. Pass `git bisect start HEAD <good-sha>` then `git bisect run ./repro.sh`; print the offending SHA in the final report.

title: git worktree for parallel branch work
body: `git worktree add ../myproj-fix feature/x` checks out another branch into a sibling directory without cloning again. Each worktree is its own working tree and index but shares .git; clean up with `git worktree remove <path>`.

title: git reflog as a safety net
body: `git reflog` is a per-branch log of where HEAD has been, including commits that were reset away or amended out. `git reset --hard <sha-from-reflog>` recovers work that `git checkout` seems to delete.

title: git sparse-checkout for monorepos
body: `git sparse-checkout init --cone` then `git sparse-checkout set dir1 dir2` checks out only the listed directories. Combine with `--filter=blob:none` partial clones to keep a monorepo's working tree tiny.

title: git signed commits require configured key
body: `git commit -S` signs with the key in `user.signingkey` of `git config`. If no key is set or gpg can't find it, the commit is refused with a non-zero exit; verify with `git verify-commit HEAD`.

title: git attributes for line endings
body: A `.gitattributes` file with `* text=auto` makes git normalize line endings on commit and restore the platform-native form on checkout. Pin specific binary extensions with `*.png binary` so git never tries to diff them.

title: git stash include untracked
body: By default `git stash` ignores untracked files. Use `git stash -u` (or `--include-untracked`) to save new files alongside your tracked changes, otherwise untracked files stay in the working tree and can confuse the next checkout.

title: git diff ignore whitespace
body: `git diff -w` (or `--ignore-all-space`) collapses whitespace-only differences when reviewing patches. Pair with `--ignore-blank-lines` for noisy refactors.

title: CI caching key per lockfile hash
body: Cache keys derived from the lockfile hash (pnpm-lock.yaml, Cargo.lock, package-lock.json) plus the OS string survive dependency edits only when the lockfile itself changes. Without the hash, every run re-downloads.

title: CI apt mirror timeouts on ubuntu
body: On Ubuntu CI a stuck apt mirror can hang the entire job; the `apt-get install` step has no default timeout. Pass `-o Acquire::http::Timeout=60 -o Acquire::Retries=2` and a sudo-level wall-clock timeout to avoid runaway bills.

title: CI cache restore failures
body: A failing cache restore must not fail the job — wrap the restore in `continue-on-error: true` and degrade to a cold cache. Audit hits via the cache step's summary; a 0% hit rate is a config bug, not an inevitability.

title: CI matrix fail-fast tradeoff
body: `fail-fast: false` on a matrix keeps running sibling jobs after one fails — useful when one slow leg's logs are the only diagnostic you need. `fail-fast: true` saves minutes on green builds.

title: CI secrets inherit between steps
body: `secrets:` and `env:` defined at the job level are visible to every step in that job unless overridden. Don't put a secret in a step env and assume it's scoped; use job-level secrets and a non-secret env for the override.

title: CI runs-on labels for self-hosted
body: Self-hosted runners match `runs-on: [self-hosted, linux, x64]` only when every label matches. A label typo silently schedules the job on a hosted runner and bursts spending.

title: CI artifact upload retention
body: Build artifacts expire after the default retention (often 7-30 days) unless you set `retention-days`. For long-lived evidence (bench results, screenshots) push them to an external bucket before the expiry.

title: CI checkout fetch-depth zero
body: `actions/checkout@v4` defaults to fetch-depth:1 (shallow). Set `fetch-depth: 0` for jobs that diff against the previous commit or run `git blame`; otherwise the log is empty.

title: CI service container healthcheck
body: A `services:` block can take a `health-cmd`/`health-interval`/`health-retries` block; the job waits for the container to report healthy before the first step runs. Without it, a half-started Postgres silently fails the first connection.

title: CI concurrency cancel-in-progress
body: `concurrency: { group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true }` cancels a superseded run when a new commit hits the same ref. Saves minutes on long branches with frequent pushes.

title: cargo workspace exclude worktrees
body: The root Cargo.toml needs `exclude = [".worktrees"]` (or each worktree listed) so cargo walking up from a worktree doesn't find this manifest and try to rebuild a package that isn't a workspace member. Without it, every worktree build fails.

title: cargo feature flag warnings fail CI
body: `-D warnings` in clippy lints force features off by default; an unused import behind a feature flag fails the whole build unless `#[allow(unused_imports)]` is scoped to the cfg. Check `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` locally.

title: cargo build script rerun-if-changed
body: `cargo:rerun-if-changed=path/to/native` in a build.rs `print!` reruns the script only when the listed file changes, not on every parent dir mtime. Without it, every build rebuilds the native crate.

title: cargo lockfile in both library and binary
body: A workspace with a library and a binary that both depend on the same crate must list it in both `Cargo.lock` views. `cargo update -p crate` updates both; `cargo update --workspace` resolves the union.

title: cargo doc rustdoc broken intra-doc
body: `#![deny(rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links)]` fails `cargo doc --no-deps` on any unresolvable link. CI should run `cargo doc --no-deps -- -D warnings` so missing backticks don't land in main.

title: cargo test no fail fast
body: By default `cargo test` stops at the first failing test in a binary. Use `cargo test --no-fail-fast` (or `--no-fail-fast` on the workspace) to run the rest and surface every regression in a single CI cycle.

title: cargo build release lto
body: `profile.release.lto = true` enables whole-program LTO and roughly halves the binary size for a CLI but takes minutes longer. Tune with `lto = "thin"` for an intermediate that still ships small.

title: cargo metadata json for tools
body: `cargo metadata --format-version=1 --no-deps` emits the workspace graph as JSON. Downstream tools that need to discover bins, targets, or features parse it instead of shelling out to `cargo build --verbose`.

title: cargo install --locked reproducibility
body: `cargo install --locked` pins the dependency graph to the crate's committed Cargo.lock. Without `--locked` an installer silently bumps to latest and may break the tool's CLI on a CI runner.

title: pip pyproject.toml sources
body: Modern pip (>= 21) reads `[tool.sources]` in `pyproject.toml` to install from a private index without a separate `--index-url` flag. CI should pin `pip>=21` and use the toml form for reproducibility.

title: pip editable install vs wheel
body: `pip install -e .` (editable) installs a link to the source so code edits are picked up without reinstall. `pip install .` builds a wheel into site-packages and is the right mode for production deploys.

title: pip-tools pip-compile upgrade
body: `pip-compile --upgrade` rewrites `requirements.txt` from the inputs in `requirements.in`. Run with `--generate-hashes` and commit the result; otherwise `pip install -r` resolves against freshest, not pinned, versions.

title: setuptools vs hatch build backend
body: Hatch (build-backend declared in pyproject) is now recommended over setuptools for new Python projects — it ships as a single static binary, handles versioning via `dynamic`, and skips the legacy `setup.py` discovery rules.

title: wheel manylinux platform tag
body: A wheel's platform tag (e.g. `manylinux2014_x86_64`) declares the oldest glibc the binary links. Manylinux2014 sets the floor at glibc 2.17 (RHEL 7 era); older manylinux tags are being phased out of PyPI.

title: pip user install vs virtualenv
body: `pip install --user` writes into ~/.local; without an active venv this is the default on Debian/Ubuntu. A misaligned venv + --user install produces ImportError on the next interpreter change.

title: pyproject requires-python guard
body: `requires-python = ">=3.10"` in pyproject stops pip from installing the wheel against an older interpreter. Add `python_requires` too for legacy setuptools backends; both are needed during the migration window.

title: pip cache dir override
source: `PIP_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/pip-cache` points pip at a writable location when $HOME is read-only (CI, containers). Pair with `pip config set global.cache-dir` to persist the override.

title: pip resolver backtracking
body: `pip` since 20.3 uses a real SAT resolver and can backtrack when constraints conflict. If a backtrack explodes the install time, split the `requirements.in` into per-feature files instead of disabling the new resolver.

title: pip dry-run install
body: `pip install --dry-run` (alias `--dry-run`) resolves and prints the would-be install set without writing to site-packages. Use it in CI to detect dependency conflicts before burning cache space.

title: docker layer cache from buildkit
body: BuildKit (BuildKit) is the default builder since Docker 23 and caches stages by their declared context. `DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 docker build .` plus `--cache-from` reuses layers across pipelines.

title: docker multi-stage named stages
source: `FROM scratch AS final` lets later stages `COPY --from=builder /out/src app/build` to a clean runtime image. Without the source/ target stages, you ship the toolchain inside the runtime image and double the size.

title: docker compose env_file vs env
body: `env_file:` in docker-compose reads `.env`-style files at start and exposes each line as an env var inside the service. `environment:` is inline; mixing them on one service silently lets `environment:` win.

title: docker volume bind mount permissions
body: A bind-mounted host directory keeps the host's UID/GID; container processes that expect a different uid produce EACCES at runtime. Bake a fixed UID into the image or `user:` the compose service to the matching one.

title: docker healthcheck vs depends_on condition
body: `depends_on: { db: { condition: service_healthy } }` waits for the healthcheck to report healthy, not just started. Without `condition`, depends_on fires as soon as the daemon returns the container ID.

title: docker network DNS round-robin
body: Docker's user-defined bridge network round-robins DNS across container replicas for the same service name. A stateful client that expects sticky sessions must use `--ip` or an explicit service alias.

title: docker stop signal vs pid 1
body: `docker stop` sends SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after the grace period. A PID 1 process that ignores SIGTERM (some shells, hand-rolled C servers) waits the whole grace for SIGKILL. Set `STOPSIGNAL` in the Dockerfile or wrap with `tini`.

title: docker context cross-host
body: `docker context use prod` switches the daemon endpoint without rebuilding images. CI runs that push to prod context first should `docker context show` to confirm the active context.

title: docker buildx cache-to type=inline
body: `--cache-to=type=inline` writes the cache manifest into the image itself (one tag, no separate cache image). For multi-arch builds use `type=registry` with `mode=max` to share across architectures.

title: docker compose profiles
body: `profiles: [ci]` in docker-compose.yml keeps a service out of `docker compose up` unless the user passes `--profile ci`. Use it for one-off jobs (db seed, load test) that should not start in a default `up`.

title: SQLite WAL mode readers don't block
body: `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` lets readers proceed while a writer holds the lock; the WAL file grows until a `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` runs. Long-lived idle connections on the reader side still see a stable snapshot.

title: SQLite busy_timeout retry semantics
body: `PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000` makes a write transaction block up to 5 s waiting for the lock instead of failing with SQLITE_BUSY. Without busy_timeout, a brief contention from a long writer becomes an immediate error.

title: SQLite prepared statement reuse
body: A prepared statement is reused by `stmt.query_map(...)` — preparing once and running N times is far cheaper than re-preparing on each iteration. Hot loops that re-prepare inside the loop show up in a `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` dump.

title: SQLite FTS5 tokenization
body: SQLite FTS5 tokenizes by Unicode categories by default; ASCII content is split on whitespace and punctuation. Use the `unicode61` tokenizer with `remove_diacritics=1` for European text; switch to `trigram` for substring search.

title: SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE upgrade
body: `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` upgrades a transaction to a write lock at BEGIN, not at the first write. Use it when the first write depends on a SELECT-then-WRITE pattern; otherwise `BEGIN DEFERRED` upgrades mid-transaction and risks SQLITE_BUSY.

title: SQLite parameter binding IN clause
body: Example code: `let placeholders = ids.iter().map(|_| "?").collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", "); conn.prepare(&format!("SELECT id FROM t WHERE id IN ({placeholders})"))?.query_map(rusqlite::params_from_iter(ids.iter()), mapper)?`. Never interpolate ids into SQL text; always bind them.

title: SQLite VACUUM rebuilds the file
body: `VACUUM` rewrites the database file to reclaim space after large deletes. It requires exclusive access (no concurrent readers) and roughly the size of the database in extra disk space; schedule during a quiet window.

title: SQLite foreign keys require pragma
body: `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` is OFF by default per-connection. A new connection inherits only the OFF default unless the pragma is set after open; FK constraints are silently skipped otherwise.

title: SQLite JSON1 functions
body: SQLite's JSON1 extension (`json_extract`, `json_set`, `json_array_length`) is built in since 3.38. It indexes JSON columns via generated columns (`GENERATED ALWAYS AS (json_extract(data, '$.k')) STORED`) for faster lookups.

title: SQLite backup API atomicity
body: `sqlite3_backup_init/step/finish` makes a hot copy of a live database without locking writers. It is incremental and survives a writer appending between steps; finish the backup before opening the copy or risk stale data.

title: HTTP API idempotency-key header
body: Idempotency-Key: <uuid> lets a client retry a non-idempotent POST safely; the server stores the result under the key and replays it on retry. Without the header, double-submits create duplicate orders / charges.

title: HTTP API 429 retry-after header
body: A 429 response includes `Retry-After:` either as seconds or an HTTP-date. Clients that ignore it busy-loop and get rate-limited longer; well-behaved clients back off to `Retry-After + jitter`.

title: HTTP API content-length vs chunked
body: A response with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` has no `Content-Length` header; clients must read until the chunk terminator. A library that bails on missing Content-Length will hang on a streaming endpoint.

title: HTTP API bearer token auth
body: `Authorization: Bearer <token>` is the OAuth-2.0 default. The token belongs in the Authorization header, not in a query string; a URL with a token in `?access_token=` leaks it through every log and CDN.

title: HTTP API CORS preflight
body: A cross-origin POST with `Content-Type: application/json` triggers a CORS preflight (`OPTIONS` with `Access-Control-Request-Headers`). A server missing the OPTIONS handler returns 405 to the preflight and the browser refuses the real POST.

title: HTTP API structured problem+json
body: RFC 9457 problem+json (`{type, title, status, detail, instance}`) is the modern replacement for ad-hoc `{error, message}`. Clients that switch on `type` (a stable contract) survive renames; switch on `message` and they don't.

title: HTTP API etag conditional get
body: `ETag: "<hash>"` plus `If-None-Match: "<hash>"` yields a 304 Not Modified on a cache hit. Servers that emit ETags without honoring the request header miss the bandwidth win and clients re-download.

title: HTTP API gzip vs brotli
body: Brotli (`Content-Encoding: br`) is 15-20% smaller than gzip on JSON / HTML but slower to encode. Use brotli for static assets, gzip for dynamic JSON where every millisecond of CPU counts.

title: HTTP API pagination cursor vs offset
body: Cursor pagination (`?after=<opaque>`) is stable across inserts; offset pagination (`?page=5&size=100`) shifts on every new row and double-sends or skips items. Use cursor in feeds, offset in static admin tables.

title: HTTP API timeout vs deadline
body: `timeout` is a per-request budget; `deadline` is the overall time the whole call must finish. A 30 s deadline with three 5 s retries budget is fine; a 30 s timeout per attempt over three retries is 90 s.

title: unit test fixture isolation
body: Each unit test must own its fixture — a shared mutable fixture across `#[test]` functions is a parallel-execution race. Use `tempfile::tempdir()` per test or wrap the fixture in a constructor that opens a fresh DB.

title: unit test naming convention
body: `snake_case` test function names describe the behavior, not the implementation: `floor_keeps_at_and_above_drops_below` beats `test_threshold`. A failure log that says `pair: error` reads as `floor_keeps_at... FAILED: assertion failed`.

title: test assert approximate float
body: Compare floats with a tolerance: `(actual - expected).abs() < 1e-4` or `f32::abs() < epsilon`. A direct `==` on floats is almost always wrong; `0.1 + 0.2 != 0.3` is the canonical example.

title: test fixture cwd tempdir
body: A test that changes the process cwd can break parallel siblings that depend on cwd-resolved paths. Use `tempfile::tempdir()` for the cwd change and restore on drop; `set_current_dir` panics on macOS sandbox failures.

title: test env var isolation
body: `std::env::set_var` races with concurrent tests in the same process. The `temp_env::with_vars` crate scopes env mutations inside a closure and restores them on drop, even on panic.

title: test assert stderr empty
body: For a clean CLI test, assert the stdout JSON AND that stderr is empty. A library that warns on every call passes `assert stdout ok` but clutters CI logs; pin it in clean assertions.

title: test ignore flaky filter
body: Marking `#[ignore]` skips a test in normal runs. Without a `#[ignore = "reason"]` and a tracking issue, an ignored test is invisible and stays broken forever; document each ignore with the issue id.

title: test coverage in CI
body: `cargo tarpaulin` and `cargo llvm-cov` produce coverage reports, but neither is in the default CI. Run them on a slow-tests lane so the report does not block normal merges, and gate new code on a coverage floor.

title: test parameterized tests
body: For data-driven tests use `rstest`'s `#[case(...)]` attribute to avoid copy-pasted functions per case. The macro generates one test per case so a failing case points at the exact inputs, not at a single body.

title: test deterministic seeds for randomness
body: Tests that exercise randomness must seed the RNG with a fixed value (e.g. `StdRng::seed_from_u64(42)`). An unseeded RNG produces a flake on the first unlucky run and the test team chases ghosts for days.

title: semantic-release commit message contract
body: Conventional commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `docs:`) drive semantic-release's version bump: feat → minor, fix → patch, `feat!:`/`BREAKING CHANGE:` → major. A commit without a type is treated as a patch by default and silently ships a patch release.

title: semantic-release release.config.js
body: `release.config.cjs` configures plugins (analyzeCommits, publish, changelog). Changing the plugin order or `preset` rewrites CHANGELOG.md; a force-pushed release-config diff on the same commits can produce a different version on the very next CI run.

title: semantic-release dry-run
body: `semantic-release --dry-run --no-ci` (or the equivalent local CLI flag) prints the version it would publish without pushing tags. Use it locally on a new branch before pushing, so a wrong preset doesn't ship a 3.x bump for a doc fix.

title: semantic-release CI mode
body: `semantic-release --ci` (or `--ci=true`) tells the tool it owns the run; without the flag local semver-less branches behave differently. CI scripts should pin `--ci` explicitly so a developer running locally does not push a tag.

title: semantic-release branch allow-list
body: `branches: ['main']` in release.config whitelists which refs release; a feature branch off main is excluded. To ship from a release branch, list `['main', {name: 'release/*', channel: 'next'}]`.

title: semantic-release tag format
body: `tagFormat: 'v${version}'` (default) prepends a `v` to every tag. Consumers pinning `v3.2.0` need to know the format; a switch to `${version}` silently breaks every install script that hardcoded `v`.

title: semantic-release analyzeCommits preset
body: `@semantic-release/commit-analyzer` with `preset: conventionalcommits` (the default) parses feat/fix/etc. Changing the preset (e.g. to `angular`) reclassifies historical commits and bumps the next release's version differently.

title: semantic-release first release
body: The first release of a repo is 1.0.0 by default; subsequent releases follow the conventional commits. To ship 0.1.0 as the initial release, add `initialVersion: '0.1.0'` in the release.config.

title: semantic-release prerelease channel
body: `prerelease: 'beta'` on a release branch publishes `1.3.0-beta.1`. The `channel` field on the branch (`next`, `next-major`, `lts`) decides which channel receives the next patch on a different branch.

title: semantic-release npm publish
body: `@semantic-release/npm` needs `NPM_TOKEN` in CI secrets. Without it, release fails after the version bump with `ENEEDAUTHENT` and the repo is left with a tag but no package; rotate the token immediately.

title: shell errexit with pipefail
body: `set -euo pipefail` in a shell script aborts on the first failure (errexit) and treats a failed command inside a pipe (`false | true`) as a failure (pipefail). Without pipefail, the script silently exits 0 on a broken first leg.

title: shell IFS word splitting
body: An unquoted variable (`$foo`) word-splits on `IFS` (default: space/tab/newline). A filename containing spaces silently becomes two arguments. Quote everything: `"$foo"` is the rule, not the exception.

title: shell xtrace debug
body: `set -x` prints each command before running it (after expansion). Pair with `set -v` for verbose readline; use `BASH_XTRACEFD=2` to send xtrace to stderr instead of stdout so a captured `$(...)` is clean.

title: shell trap cleanup
body: `trap 'rm -rf $tmpdir' EXIT` fires on normal completion, on `set -e` failures, and on signals (after redirecting them with `trap '' INT` for tests). Without a trap, a failing script leaks the fixture.

title: shell find -print0 vs xargs -0
body: `find ... -print0` and `xargs -0` together handle arbitrary filenames (spaces, newlines, quotes). Without the `-0` pair, xargs splits on whitespace and re-quotes incorrectly; filenames with a single quote break xargs silently.

title: shell subshell vs grouped command
body: `(cd /tmp && ./run.sh)` runs in a subshell — variables and `cd` do not survive. `{ cd /tmp && ./run.sh; }` is a group in the same shell; `cd` and assignments do survive. Use a subshell for isolation, a group for sequencing.

title: shell here-string vs here-doc
body: `while read -r line; do ...; done <<< "$input"` is a here-string (one arg, no temp file). A here-doc (`<<EOF ... EOF`) reads multiple lines and is right when the script body itself needs the input.

title: shell script shebang portability
body: `#!/usr/bin/env bash` finds bash in $PATH, which is fine on macOS and Linux. `#!/bin/bash` pins a filesystem path that may not exist on Alpine (musl + no /bin/bash) — use `/usr/bin/env bash` for portable scripts.

title: shell command -v existence check
body: `command -v jq >/dev/null` (not `which jq`) checks whether a command exists, portably across BSD and GNU coreutils. `which` is an external tool with inconsistent behavior on macOS vs Linux; `command -v` is a shell builtin.

title: shell job control in CI
body: `set -m` enables job control; without it, a backgrounded process (`&`) and `wait` in a non-interactive shell (CI, scripts) cannot be tracked. CI that needs to kill children on timeout uses `set -m` and `kill -- -$$`.

title: cargo workspace member path glob
body: `members = ["crates/*"]` in root Cargo.toml globs all immediate subdirectories with a Cargo.toml. A directory like `target` or `.worktrees` accidentally matched produces a phantom workspace member and a build failure.
